source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Reported (via search snippet, unverified against primary AR text) to combine natural hedges (USD receivables vs payables) with forward contracts/options, covering roughly 40-70% of near-term known FX exposures.
inr_exposure.evidence: Search-derived commentary: Zydus earns a material share of revenue from regulated markets (US ~49% of consolidated revenue per Q4FY25 segment data, per icicidirect note) and emerging markets/Europe (International Formulations grew 34% YoY to Rs 973.5cr in Q4FY25), settled largely in USD; full-year consolidated geography split not confirmed from primary source.

pli_scheme.evidence: Search-derived (third-party): 'Indian government's PLI schemes and tax incentives for pharmaceuticals have enabled capacity expansion across formulations and APIs' and 'Zydus stands strengthened by government support and can capitalize on PLI-driven local manufacturing' — not a direct AR quote, revenue impact not quantified.

china_plus_one.evidence: Search-derived (third-party/press): 'India is recognized as the fastest-growing exporter of transformers globally'; Hitachi Energy is investing ~$1.5 billion to scale global transformer production across India, China and Europe amid a global transformer supply shortage. Mentions export momentum and multi-region diversification but no AR text found explicitly framing it as 'China+1' with revenue attribution for the India entity.

govt_capex.evidence: Search-derived (press releases): highest-ever order backlog (~Rs 18,994 crore as of Dec 2024) driven substantially by a large HVDC order to transmit renewable energy from Khavda, Gujarat to Nagpur, Maharashtra, and a contract to deliver 765kV transformers to Power Grid Corporation of India Limited for grid expansion — both government/PSU-linked capex.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Search-derived (financial data aggregators): company described as 'almost debt free'; sought shareholder approval in early 2025 to raise borrowing limits to Rs 11,500 crore (Rs 1,500cr fund-based + Rs 10,000cr non-fund-based), but actual floating-rate liability share not disclosed in sources found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Search-derived: excluding the one-time large HVDC order, exports reportedly grew to over 40% of total orders in Q3 FY25, with power quality/substation/renewable orders from Australia, Indonesia, Canada, Croatia, Azerbaijan, etc. (order-book basis, not revenue basis; quarterly, not full-year).

china_plus_one.evidence: Search-derived: exports are only ~1% of turnover in FY2024-25 — an overwhelmingly domestic-focused business with no diversification/China+1 narrative found.

rural.evidence: Search-derived (third-party): company has 'over 5,000 channel partners and more than 200,000 retailers across India, providing deep penetration into both urban and rural markets'; agricultural/rural-linked cable applications saw a volume decline of ~15-16% due to pre-seasonal and monsoon impacts. No clean rural revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Search-derived (analyst note): demand supported by 'power transmission and distribution, residential and commercial construction, railways, telecommunications, renewable energy, and industrial capex'; Union Budget infrastructure capex (~Rs 11.21 lakh crore) cited as a positive policy backdrop for the Cables & Wires business.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Search-derived (financial aggregator data): company reported as having 'healthy cash, zero debt and a lean working capital cycle,' with short-term and long-term debt reported at Rs 0 mn in recent quarters, suggesting minimal floating-rate liability exposure.

crude_exposure.evidence: Search-derived: copper and PVC (a crude-oil-derived polymer) are the primary raw materials; 'rapid fluctuations in global copper prices can squeeze margins,' and margins were reportedly pressured by raw material costs and rupee depreciation toward Q4. Company manufactures its own copper rods and PVC compounds for backward integration. No explicit raw-material-cost % of revenue disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: With exports at only ~1% of turnover, direct USD revenue exposure appears minimal; possible FX exposure via imported copper cathode, but not confirmed in sources found.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI scheme continuity cited by analysts as a general sector tailwind for cables/wires demand, but no confirmation found that Finolex Cables is itself a direct PLI scheme beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: Search-derived (press/trade media): Royal Enfield exports surged 29.7% YoY to 100,136 units in FY25 (of 1,002,893 total units), driven by international market expansion; no China+1 / supply-chain-diversification framing found in sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: Search-derived (analyst commentary): analysts cite 'domestic demand aided by government-led consumption measures and a rural demand uptick' as supportive of FY25 growth; no quantified rural revenue share found.

crude_exposure.evidence: General industry knowledge (not confirmed against AR): as an auto/motorcycle manufacturer, inputs include steel, aluminum and rubber (tires, crude-linked); no company-specific % found in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Search-derived (third-party analyst note): 'Eicher's exports and CKD/CBU imports expose it to FX, but hedging policies and price realization in overseas markets moderate the net impact.' Not verified against primary AR text.
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports are ~10% of Royal Enfield unit volumes in FY25 (100,136 of 1,002,893 units); INR/USD reportedly traded in an ~82-83 band with lower volatility versus prior years (search-derived).

pli_scheme.evidence: Search-derived (third-party estimate, not an AR disclosure): under the government's Auto/Auto-Components PLI scheme (notified 2021-2024, incentives up to 13% of incremental turnover for eligible categories), one third-party analysis estimates Eicher's potential incentive receipts at roughly INR 200-600 crore over the scheme duration. Not confirmed via primary source.

ABB.report_year: CY2023 (Annual Report 2023, most recent year with a disclosed geography split found)

govt_capex.evidence: Search-derived (analyst/press commentary): 'The company remains a beneficiary of the government's capex investments in mega infrastructure and renewable projects' and is able to convert business opportunities in industrial capex (metals & mining, energy & chemicals, buildings, data centers). 'Direct exposure to government customers is minimal, with indirect exposure through EPCs at about 35% to 40%.' Not confirmed as a direct AR quote.

inr_exposure.evidence: Per AR2023 (search-derived snippet), geography by revenue was 90% Domestic / 10% Export; specific hedging policy not found in sources reviewed. Revenue by segment: 39% Electrification, 36% Motion, 21% Process Automation, 4% Robotics & Discrete Automation (CY2023, total revenue Rs 10,447 crore).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Third-party financial trackers (Tijori/SimplyWall.st) show United Spirits in a net cash position (net debt approx -₹4,060 crore as of Mar-25; debt-to-equity ~0.07), suggesting minimal floating-rate liability exposure, though the AR itself was not directly read to confirm the exact floating-rate split.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports are reported as a very small share of net sales (~0.4%), implying limited direct INR/USD translation exposure, but no explicit hedging policy statement was located.

china_plus_one.evidence: Coverage of Emcure's supply chain indicates it sources raw materials/intermediates 'primarily from China, Hong Kong, and Singapore' — i.e. a dependency-ON-China pattern rather than an AR-articulated China+1 diversification narrative attributed to revenue growth. No direct AR quote framing export growth as China+1 driven was found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company reportedly relies on a natural hedge, offsetting foreign-currency payables (trade obligations, loans) against foreign-currency receivables, rather than extensive use of derivative hedging instruments (per third-party summary, not a direct AR quote).
inr_exposure.evidence: International revenue (Europe, Canada, and other markets combined) accounted for 54% of FY2025 total revenue, up 20.5% YoY, per company commentary summarized in press coverage; explicit USD-only breakdown was not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure Pharmaceuticals is cited as one of the domestic pharma companies approved under Group B of the Government of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (outlay ₹15,000 crore, effective FY21-FY29, incentive of 4-18% on incremental sales over FY19-20 base); specific incentive amount received by Emcure was not disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (~8.3% of FY2024-25 total sales, ~₹1,405 crore) are described as mostly manufactured goods sold to other Bosch group companies, with close to 69% of exported products going to Robert Bosch, Germany (implying largely EUR-denominated intercompany exposure), per management commentary summarized in press coverage — not a direct AR quote.

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch secured approval under the Component Champion Incentive Scheme of India's PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components (approved March 15, 2022), per India-Briefing/PIB coverage; no revenue percentage attributable to PLI was disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY2025 revenue geography reported as Americas 53.9%, EMEA 34.7%, and Rest of World ~11.4% (per secondary financial-data sources, not the AR directly). 'Americas' aggregates North and South America and was mapped to export_us_pct as an approximation; it is not a pure US figure. No explicit hedging policy or USD-only exposure percentage was located.

china_plus_one.evidence: Netweb describes itself as one of India's leading 'Indian origin owned and controlled OEMs' for high-end computing systems (HPC, AI systems, servers) built under the government's 'Make in India' initiative — an import-substitution/domestic-manufacturing narrative rather than an explicit export-oriented China+1 framing with revenue attribution; company remains ~91% domestic revenue.

govt_capex.evidence: Company has secured large government-linked AI infrastructure orders, including deployment of 5,000+ GPUs for a national foundational LLM, a sovereign compute facility for CERT-IN (650+ compute units), and an NIC on-premises AI cloud order under the IndiaAI Mission (~₹1,734 crore order for Nvidia-powered servers cited in press coverage); no consolidated 'government revenue as % of total' figure was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Netweb Technologies received a PLI incentive of approximately ₹5.94 crore (₹5,93,97,758) from MeitY under the Government of India's PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware, for the period July 1, 2023 to March 31, 2024, against FY2024-25 revenue of roughly ₹1,160 crore; exact revenue percentage attributable to PLI-eligible sales was not disclosed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Anthem Biosciences is described (incl. by its own CEO Ajay Bhardwaj, quoted around its IPO) as pursuing a 'China-plus-one' strategy, having built a supply chain with minimal dependence on Chinese raw materials and positioning itself as 'the second source for many products made in China, and the first choice for new ones.' CRDMO segment (83.4% of consolidated revenue) grew 17.7% YoY to INR 17,727 Mn, with growth attributed to global pharma/biotech customers diversifying supply chains away from China.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports contributed 85% of revenue from operations, with the company serving customers across 50 countries, implying substantial foreign-currency (largely USD) revenue exposure; no specific hedging policy or currency breakdown was found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No disclosure found confirming Anthem Biosciences as an approved beneficiary of the central Bulk Drugs/API PLI scheme; its China+1 positioning as a CRDMO is a separate commercial narrative, not tied to PLI incentives in the sources reviewed.

rural.evidence: No 'rural' revenue disclosure found; company narrative instead centers on tier-2/tier-3 city expansion (Lucknow, Patna, Indore, Ranchi, Varanasi, Guwahati), noting 'demand for premium care existed outside traditional urban hubs' with ~2,700 beds being added via greenfield projects over five years. This is a tier-2 urban expansion story, not a rural-demand narrative, so no rural revenue percentage is applicable/disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: International patients revenue is disclosed separately and has run at roughly 6% of total revenue (e.g., Q4 international patient revenue grew 22.0% YoY to Rs 679 million), implying a small foreign-currency revenue base; no hedging policy disclosure found.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI schemes are not applicable to hospital/healthcare delivery services; no disclosure found. (Note: analyst estimates, not company AR disclosure, suggest ~18-22% of Medanta's revenue comes from CGHS/other government health-scheme patients, but this is payer mix, not a PLI or government-capex signal.)

rural.evidence: Company describes a pan-India network of 60,000-100,000+ retail outlets with explicit strategic emphasis on 'semi-urban and rural penetration,' and its Country Liquor segment specifically caters to price-sensitive rural consumers; no quantified rural revenue percentage was found in available sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are ENA (extra neutral alcohol, grain/molasses-based) and glass bottles/packaging; management 'cautiously monitors trends of grain prices and ENA where volatility persists,' and glass bottle price inflation of ~15-20% was cited as a margin headwind. No direct crude-oil-linked raw material percentage was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Radico derives roughly 9-10% of revenue (5-6% of volumes) from exports to 100+ countries, including growth in Africa, Asia-Pacific and airport retail; no specific hedging policy disclosure was found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme applicable to Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL)/spirits manufacturing was found; no disclosure of PLI participation.

crude_exposure.evidence: Company discloses exposure to 'normal price risks, especially in the areas of aluminium procurement and energy,' aluminium die-casting being its core process; energy price agreements were in place for CY2024-25 but 'there are no currency hedges or other long-term supply contracts' disclosed. No crude-oil-linked raw material percentage was found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Disclosed as having 'no currency hedges or other long-term supply contracts' in place (per subsidiary/consolidated annual report risk commentary).
inr_exposure.evidence: Indian operations generated ~76% of FY25 consolidated revenue (~Rs 11,560.8 crore total, +12.9% YoY) with the remaining ~24% from European operations (Italy/Germany manufacturing subsidiaries, EUR-denominated), and the company stated it carries no currency hedges.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmation found that Endurance is an approved beneficiary of the central Auto/Auto-Component PLI scheme. Separately (and distinctly from PLI), Endurance holds a Maharashtra state Package Scheme of Incentives 2019 eligibility certificate for its Waluj (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) units, enhanced to Rs 858.29 crore total eligible incentives (from Rs 606.03 crore), claimable up to Rs 125.38 crore/year from April 2025-September 2031 via SGST refund and electricity duty exemption — this is a state industrial-incentive scheme, not the central PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: NFIL has entered into long-term supply contracts with South African miners for fluorspar to 'partially de-risk itself from China' on the raw-material side. On the customer side, three marquee export customers (Bayer Crop Science, Corteva Agriscience, Fermion) rose to ~80% of exports in 1HFY26 from 63% in FY24, with CDMO revenue up sharply as global pharma/agrochemical customers scale up commercial and late-stage molecule programs with NFIL. No explicit 'China+1' phrase was located in AR-sourced snippets, so this is treated as export-momentum-plus-diversification rather than an explicit China+1 framing.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Consolidated borrowings rose from ~Rs 1,368 crore (FY24) to ~Rs 1,466 crore (FY25), largely bank term loans (~Rs 1,100 crore) funding a ~Rs 2,200 crore specialty-chemicals/HF capex program; the fixed-vs-floating split was not disclosed in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export contribution reached 77% of revenue in Q4 FY25 (quarterly figure, used as a proxy for full-year export mix since a precise FY2024-25 annual export percentage was not found), serving global pharma/agrochemical majors — indicating substantial USD-denominated revenue exposure. Specific hedging policy was not found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: A central PLI Scheme for Specialty/Advanced Chemicals (including fluorochemicals) exists, but no disclosure was found confirming Navin Fluorine as an approved PLI beneficiary or as having received PLI incentives.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company is reported to follow a near-100% gold price hedging strategy (one of the highest in the industry) to protect margins from gold price/import-cost volatility, per broker research summaries; not independently verified against the AR MD&A text itself.
inr_exposure.evidence: Titan is overwhelmingly a domestic jewellery/watches retailer; international/export business (Tanishq stores in UAE, Singapore, USA; Titan Eye+ etc.) is described qualitatively as expanding but secondary sources put total export/international revenue at under 5% of total income for FY25 (Total Income Rs 57,818 cr, +22% YoY). Figure is a third-party approximation, not a directly quoted AR percentage.

govt_capex.evidence: Company commentary and sector analysis tie SEIL's order book directly to Indian government/DISCOM T&D capex programs: the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) has ~INR 3 lakh crore committed to reduce AT&C losses, and government full-year capex outlay of ~INR 11.2 lakh crore is cited as a demand driver for the company's switchgear/transformer/vacuum-interrupter business (Systems revenue ~65% of mix). No explicit government-revenue percentage was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw materials are primarily copper, aluminium and steel (electrical/switchgear inputs), not crude-oil-linked; company disclosures flag general commodity price and geopolitical volatility as a margin risk but no crude-specific exposure was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company/management commentary (Chairman & MD remarks in the FY24-25 Annual Report materials) frames capacity expansion in explicit China+1 terms: 'the important narrative for Divi's is its unprecedented capex plans to further augment capacities besides preparing for growing opportunities arising due to the China plus one factor,' and separately, 'the China+1 strategy and global supply chain diversification efforts are further enhancing India's role as a trusted global manufacturing hub.' This explicitly ties capex/capacity growth to China+1 diversification, meeting the 'strong' bar. Note: sourced via search-engine indexing of divislabs.com PDF text, not a direct read of the PDF.

crude_exposure.evidence: Secondary summaries of the AR/MD&A note 'raw material costs, particularly solvents, remain elevated' and that 'elevated solvent costs and raw material price volatility have been exacerbated by geopolitical tensions in West Asia' along with concentrated sourcing of methanol and other Middle-East-sourced/petro-linked inputs; no specific % of raw material cost tied to crude was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (largely invoiced in USD/EUR to global pharma customers in Europe and North America) account for approximately 87-88% of gross sales in FY24-25 (Europe ~52.3% vs 40.3% in FY23; North America ~17.1% vs 28.9% in FY23), implying high foreign-currency revenue exposure, but no explicit hedging policy percentage was found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's operates in a sector (bulk drugs/APIs/KSMs) covered by India's PLI scheme for pharmaceuticals, but no source found confirming Divi's Laboratories itself is a certified PLI beneficiary or discloses PLI-linked revenue.

govt_capex.evidence: FY25 MD&A/segment commentary highlights government-programme-linked order wins: 'Water Resource Management secured significant orders across Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Jammu & Kashmir, notably under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)'; IoT-based pump solutions gaining traction under AMRUT 2.0 and JJM; Irrigation segment recorded wins from Narmada Valley Development Authority (NVDA) and the Uttar Pradesh Irrigation Department. Company also noted dispatch/execution delays tied to state-level JJM fund release timing, underscoring government-capex dependency. No specific revenue percentage tied to government orders was found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Group is reported as effectively net debt-free, with total group debt reduced to ~Rs 213 crore and liquid surplus of ~Rs 571 crore as of March 2024 (rating-agency commentary), suggesting low floating-rate-debt sensitivity, though no explicit floating-vs-fixed split was found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are pig-iron, gun metal and steel scrap, described as subject to volatile global/domestic demand-supply dynamics; no crude-oil-linked raw material exposure was identified.

china_plus_one.evidence: Narrative is mixed rather than a clean 'customers shifting from China to India' story. On one hand, Sona is India's largest importer of rare-earth magnets and, following China's export restrictions, announced plans to build domestic magnet/EV-component manufacturing to reduce China dependence ('Sona Comstar... set to start making them in India' in response to government initiatives to reduce dependence on Chinese suppliers). On the other hand, the company is simultaneously deepening China ties via a JV with China's Jinnaite Machinery to manufacture driveline systems for the Chinese market — described by outside commentary as 'a China+1 approach in reverse... not just moving away from China, but partnering within China for global advantage.' No AR MD&A quote was found directly attributing Sona's export revenue growth to global customers diversifying away from China toward India.

inr_exposure.evidence: North America (~41% of FY25 revenue per secondary analysis) and other export markets are USD/EUR-denominated, implying meaningful foreign-currency exposure, but figures are inconsistent across secondary sources (one source cites North America+Europe combined at 66% with India at 28% for a nearby period) and no official hedging policy was found; treat geography figures as approximate.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona BLW Precision Forgings (Sona Comstar) became the first automotive component manufacturer to receive certification under India's Auto PLI scheme, initially for a hub-wheel-drive motor for electric two-wheelers, and subsequently added certification for three more EV traction motor products (two e-3-wheeler motors, one e-2-wheeler motor) in August 2025. No PLI-linked revenue percentage was disclosed in available sources.
